tools.name: Nmap
tools.accepted_input: Nmap XML (-oX / -oA .xml), streamed with hardened lxml iterparse; a truncated file keeps the hosts read so far and is flagged partial. A <nmaprun scanner="masscan"> root is recorded as tool masscan.

signals.what: Scan command line, Nmap version and XML output version
signals.shown: Scans › import history; Host inspector › Discovery timeline; Scan page · Filter: scan: · Also: JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: scanner="masscan" sets tool_name masscan / scan_type port_scan; anything else is nmap.

signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page
signals.note: Epoch `start` preferred (time_source tool_run); `startstr` (scanner's local wall clock, no zone) only as fallback, flagged tool_clock.

signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page
signals.note: Same kind of value as the start (epoch vs wall clock); left NULL when <finished> is missing (truncated) or earlier than start.

signals.what: Run statistics (hosts up/down/total, elapsed, exit status, summary)
signals.input: `<runstats><finished elapsed="..." summary="..." exit="success"/><hosts up=".." down=".." total=".."/>`
signals.note: Only finished/@time|@timestr is read; the host totals nmap computed (including down hosts it did not list) are not kept.

signals.what: Scan type / protocol / port list scanned
signals.note: services is the raw port-range string (Text).

signals.what: Verbosity, debugging level, task progress, host hints
signals.note: Cleared on purpose.

signals.what: Pre-scan and post-scan NSE script output
signals.note: The stream loop has no branch for prescript/postscript, so broadcast discovery (e.g. broadcast-dhcp-discover, broadcast-netbios-master-browser) and post-scan summaries are never stored.

signals.shown: Host inspector header; Hosts list › Host column; Scan page hosts tables · Filter: ip:, subnet:/cidr: · Also: subnet/scope correlation, site grouping; Host inventory CSV
signals.note: IPv4 preferred over IPv6; one Host per IP per project (dedup). A <host> with only a MAC address is skipped entirely.

signals.what: Secondary address when a host reports both IPv4 and IPv6
signals.input: a second `<address addrtype="ipv6">` alongside the ipv4 one
signals.note: Only the first ipv4 (else ipv6) address is used.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Identity row
signals.note: Latest observation wins; never cleared by a scan that did not report it. Truncated to 64/128 chars.

signals.shown: Host inspector › State row; Hosts list › Host column state dot; Scan page current-hosts table · Filter: state: · Also: Host inventory CSV; JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: A down host with no ports, no OS match and no host scripts is skipped (not recorded as down). reason_ttl is not read. An empty reason on a later scan does not erase a stored one.

signals.shown: Host inspector header; Hosts list › Host column; Scan page current-hosts table · Filter: hostname:/host: · Also: Host inventory CSV; JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: Every hostname becomes a name observation: type PTR -> PTR record, type user -> A/AAAA, other -> SCANNER kind. The first name is the display-name candidate (source 'ptr' for PTR, else 'scanner'), applied by precedence, not last-writer-wins.

signals.input: first `<os><osmatch name="Microsoft Windows 10" accuracy="96">` and its first `<osclass osfamily vendor osgen type>`
signals.shown: Host inspector › OS row; Hosts list › Host column OS chip; Scan page current-hosts table · Filter: os:, has:eol · Also: Patterns insight: eol_os condition; Segments EOL hosts
signals.note: Only the first osmatch and its first osclass. An existing OS is replaced only by a higher accuracy; a different name is recorded as a conflict.

signals.what: Alternative OS matches, OS CPEs and OS fingerprint
Uptime, network distance, TCP/IP-ID sequence, timing
signals.input: `<uptime seconds=".." lastboot=".."/>`, `<distance value="3"/>`, `<tcpsequence>`, `<ipidsequence>`, `<tcptssequence>`, `<times srtt rttvar to/>`, `<host starttime endtime>`
signals.note: None of these host children or attributes are read.

signals.input: `<trace port=".." proto="tcp"><hop ttl="1" ipaddr=".." rtt=".." host=".."/></trace>`
signals.note: Hop addresses/names are not recorded as hosts or observations.

signals.what: Port number, protocol, state and reason
signals.shown: Host inspector › Ports table; Hosts list › Exposure chips + open count; Scan page ports table · Filter: port:, exploitport:, has:open_ports, has:cleartext · Also: Evidence web_tls / auth_smb_ad eligibility; Segments ports of interest
signals.note: Every listed port is stored, including closed ones; latest state wins. reason_ttl is not read. A port missing/invalid portid fails the whole host (savepoint rollback, counted as skipped).

signals.what: Service identification (name, product, version, extrainfo, detection method, confidence, TLS tunnel)
signals.input: `<service name="http" product="nginx" version="1.18.0" extrainfo="Ubuntu" method="probed" conf="10" tunnel="ssl"/>`

signals.what: Service CPEs, hostname/OS-type hints and service fingerprint

signals.shown: Host inspector › NSE script output; Host inspector › Ports 'Evidence' column NSE count link · Also: JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: One row per (port, script id); a later scan overwrites the output. Shown in host detail; not searchable by the host DSL and not turned into scanner observations.

signals.shown: Host inspector › NSE script output › Host scripts · Also: JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: One row per (host, script id), overwritten by a later scan.
Only the flat `output` attribute is kept, except the tables read for ssl-cert / ssl-enum-ciphers, the vulns library (vuln category) and vulners (below).

signals.input: hostscript `<script id="smb-security-mode" output="... message_signing: disabled ...">` or `<script id="smb2-security-mode" output="... Message signing enabled but not required">`
signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view; Host inspector › SMB row · Filter: vuln:, has:smb_unsigned · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: Not required or disabled becomes the scanner observation "SMB signing not required" on port 445 (the same issue NetExec reports), and sets the host's SMB signing field. Keyword match over both scripts' text.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view · Filter: vuln: · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: Scanner observation "VNC server does not require authentication" (high) on the port.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view · Filter: vuln: · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: Scanner observation "Anonymous FTP login allowed" (medium) on the port.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view · Filter: vuln: · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: Scanner observation "SMBv1 enabled" (medium) on port 445.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view; Host inspector › Ports TLS column · Filter: vuln:, has:cert_issue, certorg: · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: On http* services: the web interface's certificate fields (has:cert_issue, certorg:). On ANY TLS service, an expired certificate (judged at the scan's time) is also the scanner observation "TLS certificate expired". Self-signed is not flagged outside web ports: RDP's default certificate is self-signed. Subject CN, SANs, key and signature algorithm are not promoted.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view; Host inspector › Ports TLS column · Filter: vuln:, has:weak_tls · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: On ANY TLS service, SSLv2 / SSLv3 / TLS 1.0 / 1.1 offered is the scanner observation "Deprecated TLS/SSL protocol offered"; on http* services it also sets the web interface's weak-TLS flag (has:weak_tls).

signals.what: Cipher suites, cipher strength grades and warnings
signals.input: ssl-enum-ciphers `<table key="ciphers">` entries with `strength`, `<elem key="least strength">`, `<table key="warnings">` (e.g. 64-bit block cipher, broken cipher RC4)
signals.shown: Host inspector › NSE script output · Also: JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: Only the protocol-version keys are interpreted; weak ciphers, grades and warnings stay in the script text.

signals.what: Vulnerability scripts (vuln category: smb-vuln-*, ssl-heartbleed, http-vuln-*…)
signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view; Host inspector › Scanner observations detail · Filter: vuln:, cve: · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: Each VULNERABLE / LIKELY VULNERABLE / VULNERABLE (DoS) / VULNERABLE (Exploitable) result is a scanner observation titled as nmap titles it; severity from the text report's Risk factor, else the CVSS score; Exploitable sets has:exploit. NOT VULNERABLE and UNKNOWN are skipped. Host-rule smb-* results sit on the SMB port.

signals.input: `<script id="vulners">` tables per CPE, entries `{id, cvss, type, is_exploit}`
signals.shown: Host inspector › Scanner observations; Findings › Scanner observations view; Host inspector › Scanner observations detail · Filter: vuln:, cve:, has:exploit, exploitport: · Also: Patterns insight: vuln monoculture; promoted to a finding
signals.note: Each CVE entry is a scanner observation "<CVE> in <product> <version>", severity from its CVSS score, marked as a version match, not a test. Exploit-database entries (not CVEs) are skipped.

signals.what: Other NSE scripts (security-relevant results kept as text only)
signals.shown: Host inspector › NSE script output; Host inspector › NSE script output › Host scripts · Also: JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: Stored verbatim; not parsed, except the scripts above. X11 access, SNMP community access, risky HTTP methods, weak SSH algorithms, weak RDP encryption and empty database passwords raise no scanner observation and match no filter.

gaps: Self-signed certificates and certificate organisations are not recorded for TLS services other than http*.

Unauthenticated X11, SNMP default community, empty database passwords and other misconfigurations nmap reports (beyond VNC without authentication, anonymous FTP, SMBv1 and SMB signing) are kept only as script text.
Weak cipher suites and ssl-enum-ciphers warnings (RC4, 3DES/SWEET32, export ciphers, grades below A) are not promoted; only the protocol version drives tls_weak_protocol.
Pre-scan and post-scan scripts (<prescript>/<postscript>, e.g. broadcast discovery) are dropped entirely.
Service and OS CPEs (<cpe>) are discarded, so nmap's product identification cannot be used for CPE-based matching or grouping.
Traceroute, uptime/last boot and network distance are discarded.
The runstats host totals are ignored and down hosts without data are skipped, so a scan does not record how many addresses nmap probed and found down.
A newly created port is marked is_active=True even when nmap reported it closed (only an update recomputes is_active from state).
A <host> that has only a MAC address (no IPv4/IPv6) is skipped, and when a host has both IPv4 and IPv6 the IPv6 address is dropped.
SMB signing is keyword-matched over the concatenated text of smb-security-mode and smb2-security-mode, so SMBv1 'disabled' wins over an SMBv2 'required' on the same host.
unverified: Exact NSE output wording for the listed security scripts is from knowledge of nmap, not from repository fixtures.
Whether some UI/insight layer outside the parser later reads Script.output for specific script ids was checked only by grep for common script names (none found besides masscan-* banners).

tools.name: Nmap grepable
tools.accepted_input: nmap -oG output (.gnmap, or .txt recognised by a '# Nmap' header or 'Host: … Ports:/Status:' lines); a '# Masscan … scan initiated' header is also read, but only lines that START with 'Host:' are imported.

signals.shown: Host inspector header; Hosts list › Host column; Scan page hosts tables · Filter: ip:, subnet:/cidr: · Also: subnet/scope correlation, site grouping; Host inventory CSV
signals.note: One Host per IP per project via the dedup service; the Status: line and the Ports: line for the same host merge into one Host.

signals.input: `Host: 10.0.0.5 (router.local)` — the parenthesised name; empty `()` means none
signals.shown: Host inspector header; Hosts list › Host column; Scan page current-hosts table · Filter: hostname:/host: · Also: Host inventory CSV; JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: Recorded as a SCANNER-kind name observation (not PTR): grepable output does not say whether the name came from reverse DNS or the command line. Display name only replaces a lower-provenance one.

signals.input: `Status: Up` / `Status: Down` field on its own Host: line
signals.shown: Host inspector › State row; Hosts list › Host column state dot; Scan page current-hosts table · Filter: state: · Also: Host inventory CSV; JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: Lower-cased. A `Status: Down` line with no ports is skipped and COUNTED as a skipped host line, so a -v scan listing down hosts is reported as a partial import with a warning. Host.state_reason is always sent empty (grepable has no reason) and never overwrites an existing reason.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Ports table; Hosts list › Exposure chips + open count; Scan page ports table · Filter: port:, exploitport:, has:open_ports, has:cleartext · Also: Evidence web_tls / auth_smb_ad eligibility; Segments ports of interest
signals.note: Kept: every `open` and `open|filtered` entry (v2.416.0 — how a UDP -sU scan reports most ports), and `closed`/`filtered` entries only when they carry a service name. `closed|filtered` without a service is dropped.

signals.what: Service name (incl. ssl| tunnel prefix and ? guess marker)
signals.shown: Host inspector › Ports; Hosts list › Exposure chips; Scan page ports table · Filter: service:/svc: · Also: Evidence 'Service / version detection' + web-port eligibility; Host inventory CSV
signals.note: Stored verbatim: `ssl|http` becomes the service name 'ssl|http' and `http?` keeps the '?'. Port.service_tunnel is never set. service_conf is 0, so an nmap XML -sV identification is never overwritten by it.

signals.input: 7th subfield, e.g. `…//ssh//OpenSSH 8.2p1 Ubuntu 4ubuntu0.5 (Ubuntu Linux; protocol 2.0)/` (nmap writes product, version and extra info as one string)
signals.shown: Host inspector › Ports; Scan page ports table · Filter: version:/product: · Also: JSON / Markdown export; HTML host dossier report
signals.note: The whole combined string lands in service_version; Port.service_product and Port.service_extrainfo stay empty.

signals.input: 4th subfield (owner, only with -I/ident) and 6th subfield (SunRPC info) of each port entry
`OS: Linux 4.15 - 5.8` field on the Ports line (-O)
signals.note: Never read; only Status: and Ports: fields are parsed.

signals.input: `Seq Index: 262` and `IP ID Seq: All zeros` fields (-O)
Header `# Nmap 7.94 scan initiated …` (or `# Masscan 1.3.2 scan initiated …`)
signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page · Filter: scan:
signals.note: tool_name becomes 'masscan' for a Masscan header; scan_type 'nmap_gnmap' / 'masscan_gnmap'.

signals.input: Header text after ` as: ` (e.g. `as: nmap -oG out.gnmap -sV 10.0.0.0/24`)
signals.shown: Scans › import history; Host inspector › Discovery timeline · Also: JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: Falls back to the first '#' comment line's text when the header has no ' as: '.

signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page
signals.note: Zone-less scanner local clock, flagged time_source=tool_clock.

signals.input: Footer `# Nmap done at Mon Jul 15 10:30:25 2024 -- 2 IP addresses (2 hosts up) scanned in 24.12 seconds`
signals.note: The regex captures up to ';' or end of line; nmap's footer separates the date with ' -- ', so the captured text is not a date and Scan.end_time stays empty. Only a footer written with ';' (as in the test fixture) parses.

signals.what: Run summary (addresses scanned, hosts up, elapsed) and 'Ports scanned:' line
signals.input: Footer `-- N IP addresses (M hosts up) scanned in S seconds`; `# Ports scanned: TCP(1000;1-1000) UDP(0) …` (-v)

gaps: Nmap's footer uses ' -- ' after the date, so the scan end time is never recorded for a real .gnmap file.
The combined product/version/extra-info string is stored as the service version, leaving service product empty, so product-based views and filters see nothing from a .gnmap import.
The `ssl|` tunnel prefix is kept as part of the service name ('ssl|http') instead of setting the TLS tunnel field, so TLS services from grepable output do not read as http/TLS.
OS guesses (`OS:` field) are ignored, so a -O grepable scan adds no OS information.
A -v scan that lists `Status: Down` hosts is flagged as a partial import with a 'host lines skipped' warning even though nothing failed.

Masscan -oG output saved as .gnmap (lines beginning `Timestamp: … Host: … Ports:`) routes here, but only lines starting with `Host:` are read, so it imports zero hosts and still completes without an error.
unverified: Whether nmap escapes ', ' or '/' inside the version subfield (it substitutes '|' for '/', I believe); an unescaped ', ' would split one port entry into two and drop the tail.
Masscan -oG line shape: newer masscan prefixes each line with `Timestamp: <epoch>\t`; older versions may start with `Host:` and would then import via this parser. No masscan .gnmap fixture exists.
No real .gnmap fixture in backend/tests/fixtures; line shapes are from backend/tests/conftest.py sample_gnmap_data (which omits the rpc subfield) and knowledge of nmap's format.

tools.name: Masscan
tools.accepted_input: masscan -oX XML (<nmaprun scanner="masscan">), -oJ JSON (array or concatenated records with nested `ports`), and -oL list (`open tcp 80 10.0.0.1 <epoch>`) including greppable `Timestamp: … Host: … Ports:` lines in a .txt; --banners output in all three.

signals.input: XML `<service name="ssh" banner=…>`; JSON `ports[].service.name`; list `banner tcp 22 <ip> <epoch> ssh …`
signals.note: The banner kind is used only to name the Script row (masscan-<kind>); Port.service_name stays empty for XML, JSON and -oL imports.

signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page; Host inspector › Discovery timeline · Filter: scan: · Also: JSON / Markdown export
signals.note: XML only; masscan's XML normally has no `args` attribute (the fixture has none), so command_line is usually empty. JSON and list give no version or command line.

signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page
signals.note: Epochs converted to UTC, time_source=tool_run. `finished timestr` (local clock) is ignored on purpose; per-host `<host endtime>` is not read.

signals.what: Scan window from per-record timestamps (JSON / list)
signals.input: JSON record `timestamp`; list 5th column epoch; greppable `Timestamp: <epoch>`
signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page
signals.note: Earliest/latest record time, time_source=tool_records. Epochs on `banner` list lines are not observed.

signals.input: XML `<scaninfo type="syn" protocol="tcp"/>`, `<hosts up=… down=… total=…/>`, `finished elapsed`

signals.note: Filtered out on purpose (only open ports are inventory).

gaps: The service a banner identifies (e.g. 'ssh', 'http') is never written to the port's service name for XML, JSON or -oL imports, so masscan --banners ports show as unidentified.
The SYN-ACK reason and reply TTL masscan records per port are dropped, though Port.reason exists.
Banners are kept only as free-text script output, so an HTTP title or Server header from masscan cannot be filtered or feed web-interface views.

IPv6 addresses are stored as written (the bulk path does not normalise them), so two spellings of one address could make two hosts; no IPv6 masscan fixture.
Whether masscan XML ever writes an `args` attribute; the fixture (masscan 1.0-BETA) does not.

tools.name: Naabu
tools.accepted_input: naabu -json / -jsonl records (`{host, ip, port, protocol, tls, timestamp}`) and plain `host:port` text (also `scheme://ip:port`).

signals.input: JSON `ip` (else `host`, else `url`); text left side of `ip:port`
signals.shown: Host inspector header; Hosts list › Host column; Scan page hosts tables · Filter: ip:, subnet:/cidr:, state: · Also: subnet/scope correlation, site grouping; Host inventory CSV
signals.note: Only an IPv4 address is extracted (IPv4 regex); host state is 'up'. Each host is written in its own savepoint so one bad record is skipped, not fatal.
No hostname is passed to the host write. A text line naming a host instead of an IP (and a JSON record with only a hostname) is dropped entirely.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Ports table; Hosts list › Exposure chips + open count; Scan page ports table · Filter: port:, exploitport:, has:open_ports, has:cleartext · Also: Evidence web_tls / auth_smb_ad eligibility; Segments ports of interest
signals.note: State always 'open'. Text lines are always tcp.

signals.shown: Host inspector › Ports; Hosts list › Exposure chips; Scan page ports table · Filter: service:/svc: · Also: Evidence 'Service / version detection' + web-port eligibility; Host inventory CSV
signals.note: Only when a scheme is present; plain naabu output carries none, so service_name is normally empty.

signals.shown: Scans › import history; Scan page
signals.note: Earliest/latest record, time_source=tool_records. Text output carries no time, so start_time stays empty.

gaps: IPv6 results are dropped: the address extractor only matches IPv4, so a JSON `ip` of `2001:db8::1` or a text line `[2001:db8::1]:443` (which detection accepts) imports nothing.
`hostname:port` lines and hostname-only JSON records are dropped, and the host→IP pairing naabu reports in JSON (`host` + `ip`) is not recorded as a name observation.
naabu's `tls` flag is ignored, so ports it saw speaking TLS are not marked as such.
CDN/WAF attribution (`cdn`, `cdn-name`) is ignored, so a CDN edge address is indistinguishable from the real host.
unverified: No naabu fixture in backend/tests/fixtures; key names (host, ip, port, protocol, tls, cdn, cdn-name, timestamp) are from knowledge of naabu v2 output.
Whether naabu ever emits a `scheme` key; the parser reads it but I know of no naabu option that writes it.
Some naabu versions may nest `port` as an object; `int(port)` on a dict would raise outside the per-host savepoint and fail the whole import.
